gbm_population_evidence.quote: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma patient with definitive resection prior to enrollment

candidate_evidence.quote: The investigational vaccine (MT-201-GBM) in this study is made from a type of immune cell called monocytes, which have been engineered to express a cytomegalovirus (CMV) protein.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma patient with definitive resection prior to enrollment

role_evidence.quote: monocytes isolated from patient's leukapheresis loaded with CMV pp65-LAMP (Lysosomal-associated Membrane Protein) mRNA (Messenger Ribonucleic Acid)

agents.drug_class_hint: autologous monocyte cell vaccine loaded with CMV pp65-LAMP mRNA

agents.agent_name_registered: temozolomide (standard radiation plus temozolomide and dose-intensified cycle; not a registered intervention)

role_evidence.quote: After leukapheresis, patients receive standard radiation therapy combined with temozolomide for about 6 weeks, followed by one cycle of temozolomide for 21 days.

source_quote.quote: MGMT promoter unmethylated (Determined by Caris Life Science pyrosequencing);

coder_notes: Only investigational intervention is an autologous mRNA-loaded monocyte vaccine (cell therapy / vaccine), an excluded type. Temozolomide listed as backbone because the description states all patients receive it. Primary outcome includes pp65 T-cell immune response (immunogenicity of the vaccine), which is not a candidate drug.
